body:
Handoff and continuity rules for TermAl (Termal::Fable2, 2026-11-13 at about 03:40Z, rev 2). They answer Greg (Asistant 588693a8 #1497/#1498/#1500): „reguly przekazywania dalej sesji musza byc precyzyjne”.
CAUSE (corrected with Opus2 #5804): the landing train was NOT stalled. FULLs were running on runners that the session list doesn't show as active: DL560 Codex 6, Central and s4, with landings every ~40 min. The real gaps were these. (a) The coordinator left free Sol/Opus coders without assignments. (b) c593's R1 request never reached Opus2. (c) Mail sent to a listed display name routes to a domain mailbox and doesn't wake the recipient (w-ee0454f76b19).
RULES, with no new gates:
1. WHO to WHOM. Coordinator → coder: assignment. Coder → Opus2: READY or a placement request. Opus2 → coder: GO or a result. Coder → coordinator: done or blocked. Coordinator → Greg: only via Asistant.
2. TRIGGER. Every message ends with "NEXT: <owner> <action>". Whoever finishes a step starts or requests the next in the same turn. When a coder finishes an item, the coordinator assigns the next ready item in that turn.
3. DELIVERY (rev 2, after Asistant #1503). Address by the exact native id from the start: session-N, or host:UUID::session-N for remote roots, NEVER a display name. A receipt isn't delivery, and durableButNotWoken alone doesn't prove a missed wake: check the exact messageId's current status with termal_read_mailbox_message. If it's still unresolved, retry only with the IDENTICAL message, key and route. Never switch the route or mint a new intent to replay it. If a message went to a wrong route, leave it there. Tell the recipient natively that it exists, by mailbox and message id, without restating its content. Then the recipient reads and answers it.
4. NO REACTION. After 20 min, ping once natively. After 40 min, the coordinator reassigns or takes it over and records why.
5. PARALLELISM. A running FULL never blocks reviews, author runs on other runners, or code writing. Opus2 places them alongside, within the Central budget. Opus2 confirmed this as in force (#5806).
6. WATCHDOG. Fable2 runs a 30-min cron at :13 and :43 that checks every coder has work or a named next owner, and assigns from the ready Greg-reported backlog.

REV 3 (2026-11-13, 03:50Z), after Greg (Asistant #1507): „To jest ważne, prace muszą iść cały czas. Bez watcher'a czy mojego 'status'.” Continuity must come from the normal flow, NOT from a periodic watcher or Greg asking for status. Changes:
7. QUEUE DEPTH 2 (primary mechanism). Every coder always holds its current item plus a named NEXT item, given by the coordinator up front, so finishing one item needs no coordinator round-trip. While the current item waits on a slot, review or gate, the coder does the NEXT item's read-only plan. It claims the NEXT item once the current one is in review or gate. On finishing an item, the coder starts NEXT at once and tells the coordinator, who then tops the queue back up to two in that same turn.
8. Rule 4 (no reaction) is checked IN FLOW, not by a timer. Every session, on every wake, first scans its own outstanding requests. If one has had no visible reaction for over 20 min, it pings once natively. Over 40 min, it hands the request to the coordinator, who reassigns it or takes it over.
9. Rule 6 (watchdog cron) is DEMOTED to a safety net only. Nothing depends on it; it should find nothing to do. If it does find an idle coder or a stalled request, that is a process defect: the coordinator fixes the flow, not just the instance.
Initial queues set at about 03:48Z:
- c593: w-6930, then w-aa3d5636c295.
- d50d: w-93b7 and w-70ed, then w-1a94544b753a.
- edfd: the 36d0 and 4fad evaluations, then w-79f213be4f9e.
- a7bb: the 78ec closure, then w-ee0454f76b19.
- 03d4: w-277b, then w-fd84 with the w-492e slice.
- 8e1f: w-56cd, then w-eca76d70bca9.
- Opus3: w-7845, then w-aa0121f4066c.

REV 4 (2026-11-13, 03:52Z), after Asistant #1509/#1510: Greg's „Bez watcher'a” also excludes a watcher as a safety net. Kimi::Consultant's independent review is at mailbox-125b6704… #163. Changes, which SUPERSEDE rules 4, 6, 8 and 9 above where they conflict:
- Rule 6 (watchdog) is REMOVED. Fable2's recurring cron 83a1b496 was deleted at 03:52Z. There is no periodic watcher of any kind.
- Rules 4 and 8 are reworded. The 20/40-minute thresholds are NOT a promise of timed action, because nothing fires without a wake. They apply only when a session is woken for some other reason. At that point it first checks its own outstanding COORDINATION requests (an assignment, a placement request, GO or READY), not a healthy run that is still going. A request past 20 minutes gets one native ping; one past 40 minutes goes to the coordinator.
- An "idle" status in the session list does NOT prove inactivity: runs execute on runners. Before reassigning anything, check three things:
  (1) the exact messageId's current status (termal_read_mailbox_message);
  (2) the run's state;
  (3) the item's claim and fence.
  Then use the supported handoff or claim recovery, never a parallel claim.
- Every NEXT line names the item and the concrete dependency or result it waits on (a run id, a commit, a review), not just an owner.
- Continuity comes only from the normal flow: queue depth 2 (rule 7), push handoff where the finisher wakes the next owner, and resource owners sending the next GO on each END.
KNOWN LIMIT, reported to Kimi: if a wake is lost, nothing notices until some other mail wakes the sender or the recipient. The causes are product defects being fixed: w-ee0454f76b19 (sends by display name aren't woken), w-80e0cb2002da (a stop pauses the queue and holds wakes) and w-eb21662dce0a (an unresolvable Claude turn end pauses the queue). Until they land, the guard against them is native ids and checking the receipt.

REV 5 (03:53Z), applying Kimi::Consultant #228 exactly:
- Before any ping or reassignment, check four things: the exact message's currentStatus, the recipient's ACK (its processedThrough in that mailbox), the run's actual terminal state, and the claim and fence.
- Reassign only through the supported Engram handoff (offer, then accept) or through claim recovery after the claim lapses, never as a plain new assignment.
- NEXT includes the dependency's id: run id, root generation, fence or commit.

REV 6 (03:54Z): this TermAl memory MIRRORS the shared Engram memory rules-push-handoff-2026-11-13, rev 3. Where the two differ, the shared one governs. The recurring :13/:43 cron was deleted at 03:52Z. The only scheduled wake allowed is a one-shot for a named event at a fixed time. Example: the one-shot for the rollback-hold review at about 08:57Z on 11-13.

REV 7 (03:56Z), after Kimi::Consultant #232. Event coverage is ONLY these existing backend events:
- resume_after_test_runs;
- delegation fan-in;
- the native mailbox wake;
- an Engram offer/accept followed by an explicit native mailbox wake.
"Handoff" in this memory means an Engram offer/accept plus a native wake. It does NOT mean TermAl's handoff-ledger watchdog, which polls every 2 s and is excluded as a fallback.
EXPLICIT RECOVERY GAPS, not automated, and fixed only when they actually occur:
- display-name sends (w-ee0454f76b19);
- Stop/pause holding the queue (w-80e0cb2002da);
- failed or unresolvable runtime turns (w-eb21662dce0a);
- pre-start acknowledged continuations;
- offline peers;
- a waking owner that is missing.
The 15-min scheduled wake in rules-waits-and-wakes-greg-act-holds-2026-11-12 conflicts with Greg's no-watcher word, so an amendment was proposed jointly with Engram::Fable. Until then: no drain before Greg says ready; never block independent work; resume on concrete events; no timer.
